label: S. 320

other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 320, National Earthquake Hazard Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2025

summary: This bill reauthorizes the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program through fiscal year 2028 and expands the responsibilities of participating federal agencies. It adds tribal governments to program activities, emphasizes post-earthquake functional recovery and infrastructure resilience, addresses secondary hazards like tsunamis and fires, and sets specific funding authorizations for federal agencies involved in earthquake research and mitigation.

affected_groups.effect: Must execute expanded program duties, coordinate emergency broadcasts with the FCC, provide technical assistance to tribal governments, and report biennially on implementation recommendations.
Eligible for technical assistance regarding building inventories, seismic performance evaluations, cost-effective retrofitting, and evacuation plan creation.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes appropriations for the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program and specific agencies including the U.S. Geological Survey, National Science Foundation, and National Institute of Standards and Technology through fiscal year 2028.
Expands program activities to explicitly include tribal governments alongside state and local governments.
Requires federal agencies to improve understanding of and develop resilience measures for secondary earthquake hazards such as tsunamis, landslides, liquefaction, and structural fires.
Directs agencies to focus on post-earthquake functional recovery to maintain or restore buildings and lifeline infrastructure systems like water, electricity, and transportation.
Coordinates earthquake early warning systems with the Federal Communications Commission for rapid and reliable broadcasting in predominant regional languages.
Directs that cancelled or unused appropriated funds under this act be transferred to the general fund of the Treasury for deficit reduction.
missing_information: The total aggregate economic impact across all private sectors or specific non-federal entities cannot be determined from the text.
Long-term outcomes of specific technical assistance provisions remain dependent on future appropriations.
summary_detail.plain_summary: This bill reauthorizes the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program through fiscal year 2028 and expands the responsibilities of participating federal agencies. It adds tribal governments to program activities, emphasizes post-earthquake functional recovery and infrastructure resilience, addresses secondary hazards like tsunamis and fires, and sets specific funding authorizations for federal agencies involved in earthquake research and mitigation.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation updates and extends federal earthquake mitigation and research frameworks across four federal science and emergency management agencies through 2028, adding tribal participation and shifting focus toward functional recovery and secondary hazards.
